summary: F-010 and F-011 are closed as originally stated: P3 now freezes 14 exact before/after hunks plus a patch, with no-touch covering Execution Mode, §3a, DISPATCH identifiers, generated regions, KIMI_DETACHED_CAPS and context-window guidance; P4’s distinguishing cases now match only the ad-video reorder. Independent hunk review found no change to dispatch/inline contracts, blueprint skip/mandatory semantics, receipt fail-closed behavior, registries, station lists, fixtures, or tests, and no Sol/Grok session mapping copied into defaults. Residual issues are documentation consistency, not those contracts: CLAUDE.md still contains an untouched unconditional Sonnet 5 pin immediately after the new ‘registry defaults, not live session’ callout, and model-routing.md still contains adjacent hardcoded profile/model sentences outside the frozen hunks. Those leftovers are inexact remaining-scope, not executor-invented P3 text. This advisory review is not an implementation or release receipt. D1–D12 stay parked; no dispatch packet is required in this planning request.

findings.claim: The frozen P3 hunks leave an immediate CLAUDE.md contradiction: the new callout says the generated table is not a live assignment, while the next untouched paragraph still says svc-default pins EXEC/REVIEW to Sonnet 5 and that pin is what runtime honors today.
findings.analysis: F-010 is closed for executor invention: every intended P3 edit is now an exact before/after hunk, the patch matches those 14 hunks, and the listed no-touch regions (Execution Mode, WI-386/WI-347, §3a, DISPATCH=mimo-pro|sonnet, generated blocks, KIMI_DETACHED_CAPS, context-window guidance) are absent from the patch. The remaining defect is incomplete replacement of the same class of unconditional pin inside a file that P3 does edit. After hunk 5, CLAUDE.md would read: heading ‘Registry Defaults’; generated svc-default table; new prose that the table is not a live session assignment and must be resolved via resolve-model.sh; then the original next paragraph, which is not in the hunk list, still asserting that svc-default pins EXEC and REVIEW subagents to Sonnet 5 and that ‘the model pin is what runtime honors today.’ A later dispatch implementer applying only frozen hunks will publish both sentences. That does not change resolver, dispatch-policy, reviewer-policy, or generated bytes, but it reintroduces the stale-unconditional-pin failure mode P3 claimed to remove, inside the one file whose heading and callout were rewritten to deny that reading. This is unresolved consequential wording in the resulting document (rubric 10), not a demand to implement D12 or to certify a dispatch packet.
